text: She hadn't eaten since morning and sat in the tally room, checking numbers, stomach knotting as the editor watched her.
She'd eaten dinner before her shift and sat in the tally room, checking numbers as the editor watched her closely.
At the handler's post, she called each command clearly, steady despite the ache under her ribs, whistle sharp against the morning wind.
At the handler's post, she called each command clearly, steady after a full breakfast, whistle sharp against the morning wind.
You sit at the pool's edge instead of crouching, coaxing your niece through one more lap, cheering when she touches the wall.
You crouch at the pool's edge, coaxing your niece through another lap, cheering when she touches the wall.
He logged the pump pressure, turned at the galley bell, and handed the watch to the next man.
He logged the pump pressure, radioed the bridge, and handed the watch to the next man.
She tuned the last string, checked the pedal, and eyed the parents' biscuit plate before waving the child through.
She tuned the last string, checked the pedal, and waved the first child through the curtain.
The contractor worked the case reset slowly, wiping his hands, pausing to steal glances at the trays of trimmed meat.
The contractor worked the case reset briskly, wiping his hands, pausing only to check the clock on the wall.
At the landing he swung the loader through the piled logs, arms trembling, breath short, the thermos left cold since dawn.
At the landing he swung the loader through the piled logs, arms loose, breath even, the thermos coffee still warm inside him.
The supervisor arranged each offering fast, watching the clock, and rang the bell a little early.
The supervisor arranged each offering by hand, careful and slow, and rang the bell right on time.
She took her stance, released the bowl, and glanced at the tea board as it curved toward the jack.
She took her stance, released the bowl, and watched carefully as it curved slowly toward the jack.
You grab the wrench yourself, thread the coupling, and gulp water from the jug before calling out the depth.
You grab the wrench yourself, thread the coupling, and call out the depth as the core comes up.
He sorted the parcels fast, stomach hollow since the morning shift, stacking bins without once checking the clock.
He sorted the parcels fast, adjusting the strap on his apron, stacking bins without once checking the clock.
The substitute hung drywall panels in the corridor slowly, arms trembling, distracted by the crew's midmorning meal smell.
The substitute hung drywall panels in the corridor efficiently, arms strong, energized after the crew's midmorning meal.
The trainee dropped the puck, skated clear, and pocketed the mints the timekeeper offered without waiting to be asked twice.
The trainee dropped the puck, skated clear, and watched the play develop from the top of the circle.
She knelt at the bed, pressed each bulb to the marked depth, and took the offered biscuit before the volunteer finished asking.
She knelt at the bed, pressed each bulb to the marked depth, and moved the trowel down the row in steady sequence.
On the last piece she dug into the water, legs driving hard, stomach hollow, pulling clean through every stroke.
On the last piece she dug into the water, legs driving hard, full from breakfast and pulling clean through every stroke.
On the street corner, the apprentice held the microphone steady, distracted, watching the food cart across the street.
On the street corner, the apprentice held the microphone steady, checking its cord, waiting for the next passerby to stop.
At the signing table, her nephew stacked the books slowly, stomach tight, counting the minutes until the break for food.
At the signing table, her nephew stacked the books neatly, chatting with fans, checking the stack count for the afternoon.
He stacked the graded quizzes and reached for the next one, catching the crinkle of a wrapper across the room.
He stacked the graded quizzes and reached for the next one, ignoring the chatter from the other side of the room.
She'd skipped breakfast at the terminal café and stood stamping passports through the long, slow shift, stomach hollow.
She'd had a big breakfast at the terminal café and stood stamping passports through the long, slow shift.
She stacked the chairs four high, unsure of the weight, and left the trolley for someone else to push.
She stacked the chairs six high, quick and sure, and pushed the trolley back to the storeroom herself.
